typical_symptoms: Yellowing of the midrib on the lower surface of mature leaves
Progressive chlorosis extending from the midrib into the adjacent leaf blade lamina
Premature drying and necrosis of leaf tissue starting from the tip and margins
Stunting of the overall cane growth under severe infections
Internal discoloration or pinkish-red internal stalk tissue in some advanced stages or specific cultivars
visual_characteristics: Distinct bright yellow to yellowish-orange discoloration strictly localized along the midrib
Sharp color contrast between the yellow midrib and the remaining green or progressively yellowing leaf blade
Accumulation of honeydew and subsequent black sooty mold on the leaves due to insect vector activity (aphids)
Bunching or curling of top leaves in severe cases
lesion_characteristics: Generalized chlorosis rather than distinct discrete lesions or spots
Diffused longitudinal discoloration running parallel to leaf veins
No well-defined necrotic borders in early stages, transitioning to broad necrotic tip-dieback
color_characteristics: Bright yellow to golden-yellow along the midrib
Gradual transition from yellow midrib to green leaf blade, later turning straw-colored or brown upon tissue death
Reddish or pinkish tinges sometimes developing on leaf sheaths or midribs depending on the cultivar
texture_characteristics: Dry and papery as the chlorotic tissue progresses to necrosis
Sticky in areas infested by aphid vectors due to honeydew secretion
Smooth leaf surface lacking pustules, raised scabs, or velvety spore masses
spatial_patterns: Longitudinal parallel streaks along the midrib and vascular bundles
Symmetrical yellowing originating from the leaf collar and extending toward the tip along the midrib
Systemic distribution affecting lower to mid-canopy leaves predominantly
distinguishing_features: Yellowing is heavily concentrated on the lower surface of the midrib while upper leaf surfaces may initially remain greener
Absence of fungal fruiting bodies, necrotic ring spots, or eye-shaped lesions
Association with heavy populations of the sugarcane aphid vector (Melanaphis sacchari)
commonly_confused_with: Root rot or drought-induced premature senescence
